summary: The core is built as a scan-time video pipeline driven by the board's own H/V counters: tile layers fetch and shift pixels on H[2:0] phases, sprites are found per line by a Y-adder comparator and drawn into ping-pong line buffers, and layer priority is a per-pixel mux into palette RAM. It also models board behavior MAME does not, such as the OKOUT-triggered bus-request sprite DMA, CPU wait states on video RAM access, and palette-RAM address contention during active video. MAME's draw_sprites/screen_update decomposition and its tilemap callbacks do not appear. The only clearly MAME-like detail is the bank-select expression.

findings.note: H counts 0x80..0x1FF and V reloads to 250 after 511, so the 9-bit counter ranges give 384x262 the way the board's counters do. Blanking, HINIT and a two-line-early LVBL_obj are decoded from counter values. MAME only gives zero-based raw screen parameters.

A write to OKOUT starts a state machine that asserts bus_req to the 6809's BREQ, waits for bus_ack during vblank, and copies 0x180 bytes with a counter at 6 MHz while the CPU is halted. MAME instead copies the buffer instantly on the write.

findings.signal: per-line sprite search with adder comparator
findings.note: On each line the sprite table is scanned in steps of 4. A match is computed as &Vsum[7:4] of Y + ~VF (an adder chain), and up to 24 matching entries go into a per-line object buffer, written in reverse slot order. This is the board's line-based sprite pipeline, not MAME's whole-frame loop from the end of spriteram drawing with transpen.

findings.signal: ping-pong pixel line buffers with flip by XOR
findings.note: Pixels are written into two line buffers that swap each line and are cleared on readout. Screen flip is done by inverting the buffer address bits ({AW{flip}}^posx) and complementing VF, rather than MAME's arithmetic 240-sx / 240-sy.

findings.signal: pixel-phase tile fetch and shift registers
findings.note: The tile RAM is read at a fixed H[2:0] phase, the ROM address is built from ID, flip and V bits, and the data drives bitplane shift registers that shift left or right by hflip at each pixel. There is no tile_info callback or decoded-tile abstraction.

findings.signal: scroll as H/V adders latched on tile boundary
findings.note: Scroll is the hpos/vpos register added to the flipped H/V counters (Hsum, VS). The upper bits are reloaded only when the low three bits roll over, which is how a counter-adder scroll circuit behaves. MAME just calls tilemap set_scrollx.

findings.signal: CPU wait states on video RAM access
findings.note: char_busy and scr_busy stall the 6809 when it accesses tile RAM outside the allowed H phase. This bus contention is not modeled in MAME's address map.

findings.signal: palette RAM address mux and contention
findings.note: In active video the palette RAM address comes from the pixel mux, and the CPU address is used only in blanking. A CPU write during active video drives the CPU data straight onto the RGB output. Chip selects can be gated by ~LVBL. These are hardware side effects that MAME's palette_device write does not reproduce.

findings.signal: per-pixel priority mux instead of layered draw passes
findings.note: One registered mux chooses char, then sprite or scroll per pixel, using the scrwin attribute bit and scroll pens 0 and 6. The pen rules have to match MAME's transmask (neutral). The structure, though, is a pixel-time selector, not MAME's four ordered draw calls.

findings.signal: sound IRQ from vertical counter bit
findings.note: The Z80 interrupt is taken from V[5], so it is derived from the raster counter. MAME uses an abstract 240 Hz periodic timer.
The test bank==3'd4 ? special : bank[1:0] has the same special case as MAME's 'if (data == 4) set_entry(4) else data & 3', not a decode of individual latch bits.

The decode is a hierarchical case on A[15:13], A[12:11] and A[10:8], like 138-style decoders, and the flip/sound-reset latch is indexed by A[2:0]. The resulting memory map is identical to MAME's, as it must be.
